newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gilts to push ahead to 111-20.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gilts to push ahead to 111-20.

text.p: June gilt futures are buoyed by strength in other bond markets and by post-election euphoria and are likely to push higher on Tuesday, technical analysts said.
"We are in a sharp upward channel which brings in resistance at 111-20," said Elli Gifford, independent technical analyst near Cambridge.
The June contract jumped higher at the open. At 0707 GMT, it was trading at 111-11, 7/32 above Friday's close. Monday was a market holiday.
Tuesday's low of 111-10 was also Friday's high and marked the break of an initial resistance level, analysts said.
"The real resistance is at 112-00," said Gifford.
A landslide victory for the opposition Labour party in Thursday's election is underpinning the market, analysts said.
"We should go about 10 ticks higher today," said Richard Adcock, manager, technical research, at HSBC Futures in London.

The British Treasury earlier said its monetary meeting was brought forward to 0700 GMT from the scheduled Wednesday slot, and that Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown would make a statement at 1000 GMT.
"The view that there will be an emphasis on fiscal tightening is helping the market," said Adcock.
Some market players are anticipating a half point rise in interest rates after the monetary meeting, but most expect only a quarter point.
Support for the June gilt contract is at Friday's low of 110-05, Gifford said.
"But it's highly improbable it will be retested," she added.
September short sterling futures dropped four basis points after the announcement of an earlier than anticipated monetary meeting, but have room to climb to 93.15, analysts said.
September short sterling was trading at 93.09 at 0722 GMT.
